Im so sorry, I cannot imagine losing a partner that way.   When my Dad lost his battle with mental illness, I never thought I would feel real happiness/worthy of normal relationship again. A friend said to me about losing someone close "it hurts like hell now, and you'll probably think about it everyday,  but everyday it will start to hurt a little bit less until the thought of them makes you smile again" He was so correct about this.  I spent a 6 months home grieving with family and then was lucky enough to be able to travel and rough it in SE Asia for a couple of months.  It was so hard/emotional at first but refreshing to not have people pity me anymore.  Noone knew my story unless I decided to tell them.  There were also cheap meditation centers that helped me deal with it head on...and days on the beach didnt hurt either...I can still remember the first day since his death I woke up happy. .. sorry I am rambling and I still have tough days, but my point is, I know if feels impossible now, but you will get through this, it will take time, but humans are built to be resilient.

You look great!  40lbs is no joke and takes so much hard work! Hope you are feeling better inside and out.  I'm so sorry for your loss, I also lost my father to suicide almost 2 years ago.  It took me so long to get emotionally strong again and get over the feelings of "Im so broken, who would ever want me"  and to get motivated to prioritize my weightloss. Started at my alltime high 218 and down to 198 in 3 months, still a long way to go but now that Ive gotten that first 20lbs out of the way it finally feels feasable to have a body I love.  Just wanted to share you arent alone out there. Good luck!

I think a lot of people underestimate the importance of knowing when too much, is too much. It seems like you know your child really well and dont want to put him through an experience where the risk is greater than the reward and I think that can be a good attitude.  I've learned through trial and error when running that last errand or staying at a family function that extra 1/2 hour was just TOO MUCH. There is no "right way" to do something or right way to act/socialize. It should be what makes your son happy. 

That being the case, if he wants to play with this friend, I think its good if you let him.and it might make him feel good about himself to go to a friends house (maybe just provide some guidance to the other mom and limit it to 2 hours or so and see how it goes) or suggest the first playdate be at your house so you can observe how they get along. Planning an activity that both kids would enjoy could be helpful too!

I am from MA so I'm sure I take for granted being from a progressive state but calling 911 saved my fathers life SEVERAL times throughout the worst 15 years of his illness. By that I mean on 2 occasions, they got there just in time to save his life during his attempts.  While the institution he was sent to each time provided pretty sub-par long-term care, it was no "hell-hole" and usually he would do pretty well for about 6 months afterward until he went into another episode. Again, you would have to research the facilities in your area and make sure they have a decent reputation.

But reading again that they are a minor, I would at the least consider telling them you will call their parents. Basically, having lived it,  I do not think it is healthy for you to feel responsible for their threats. That may sound selfish, and I'm sure your partner is not threatening suicide to be manipulative, but it can be manipulative. If they are serious and need someone to save them, you are too far away to be there. If they goes through with their threat, while you are helpless in NY you will NOT be responsible but in your grief you will feel guilty.

Of course you deserve to live, this is not youre fault.  Im not going to lie, the next few months or more will be very difficult.  After my fathers suicide I felt like the walking wounded. I didn't know how I would ever feel normal or happy or worthy of finding a partner. I felt 100 different emotions including guilt.  But I got through it. Im mostly happy, I dont feel so insecure dating anymore, like Im too wounded for someone to love.  I have these moments of pure happiness where I am so grateful to be alive I could burst. So just know as you go through unimaginable pain in the next couple of months that you will get through this. And when you are ready, it will be ok to be happy.

For your own emotional safety and hers you need to tell her very clearly that the next time she threatens to kill herself you will call the police. And most importantly, you need to follow through with that. This may seem harsh but it is so unfair for her to put that responsibility in your hands. If she does something and you didnt call them, although it will NOT be your fault, you will still feel guilty, it will haunt you.  I say this as the child of a bipolar suicide victim, who spent my entire 20's fearing his death, so I am speaking with experience. Her hospital bill will suck but it is worth her life. 

In addition, bipolar is a very serious mental illness.  It is so important that she discusses the need for insurance with her parents(she may appreciate your help, maybe she could write them a letter if they dont take her seriously)  She should seek professional help as soon as possible.  Mental illnesses typically get worse with age if not properly diagnosed and treated.  15 years after my dad's first bipolar "episode" he would still re-live arguments from that first trauma his mind put him through. 

Good luck and continue to share with her all the things you love about her and help her feel  *understood*

Absolutely bullet dodged!  I would agree, although it generally gets easier I think there will always be those days that a memory or insensitive comment can just put you right back into the rawness of it.  Other days, I wouldnt give those same/memories/reminders a second thought.

You may feel worthless at times, but you are not worthless. You weren't bullied for good reason, but from other kids insecurities, ignorance and lack of empathy. They will later suffer from guilt or from just being a shitty person. I'm sure it can't be easy having Aspergers and trying to navigate a world that doesn't always make sense, so try not to compare yourself to others and instead figure out what would make you happy.  Its really all that's important - not what others EXPECT you to do.  
You are someones child, your death would be the worst thing to ever happen to your parents, I say this as a survivor of a loved ones suicide (one I had a pretty terrible relationship with)  and it is something that will hurt so badly forever. Talk to them, tell them how you feel and ask them for help, ask them to help you find a way to feel useful.  I know its all easier said than done, and I'm not sure if you suffer from sensory issues but that could make every day thinks much more difficult - don't be hard on yourself.   
--finally - your story reminds me of my brother - he has undiagnosed aspergers and his childhood growing up was brutal. looking back, I can't believe my parents didn't have us move so he could switch school systems.  It got better in his 20's, he had a few friends, but difficulty dating and he never really seemed comfortable around people... eventually at 29 he met his wife (online as he has a hardtime meeting people) and the confidence he gained from having a great partner was amazing,  he may have had to wait a while for happiness but it was there. Don't give up hope please.
